Brent and WTI are Friday's closing levels. The pound is the CBE's Thursday rate. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: October's urban inflation rate (one headline gives 12.7% but its page returned 403), so the brief uses the nationwide rate; Brent's weekly loss, about 13.2% for front-month futures in Bloomberg against more than 12.5% in See News; Thursday's breadth, where See News and Youm7 (169 up, 40 down) differ from Youlyou (173 up, 38 down), so the chart uses the two that agree; Thursday's turnover (EGP 10.1 bn to 10.2 bn against 9.5 bn); Goldman Sachs' current fair-value level for the pound, not given; the split of reserves between foreign currency and gold, not reported; Brent against the budget's oil assumption, not re-verified.

items: Cabinet orders three months of spending cuts: government electricity use down 20%, vehicle fuel down at least 30%, and no new projects or car purchases → the state is cutting its own fuel and dollar needs, a sign of fiscal strain but also of lower demand for FX.

The pound ends the week at EGP 54.01 per dollar at the CBE, with the dollar down about 2.12 pounds (3.78%) over the week → foreign money returns to Egyptian T-bills, and one banker sees 50 to 52 if inflows last.
Brent ends Friday at $98.32 as oil futures post their biggest weekly drop since 2022 → Gulf exports recover and traders bet on a faster end to the Iran war, which eases Egypt's import bill.
EGX30 ends the week at 51,152.73, up about 4.9% from Sunday's close (derived) after three straight gains → the pound's rally and falling oil bring buyers back; market cap reaches EGP 4.05 tn.

EGX30 rises 0.99% to 51,152.73 on Thursday, its third straight gain, with 169 stocks up and foreigners the only net buyers → a firmer pound and lower oil bring foreign money back; market cap reaches EGP 4.05 tn.

The pound strengthens to EGP 54.01 per dollar at the CBE on Thursday evening, after 54.77 on Wednesday → foreign investors turn net buyers of Egyptian T-bills ($112.3 mn on Wednesday) as oil falls, easing dollar demand.
Net international reserves reach a record $57.5 bn at end-October, up about $152 mn from September → a record buffer gives the CBE more room to support the pound as the IMF programme nears its end.

Brent rebounds 3.9% to $98.29 on Thursday after tanker attacks in Hormuz, a day after an 8.7% fall → Iran says Hormuz stays shut until its seven conditions are met, so oil swings remain a risk to Egypt's import bill.

Brent settles 8.7% lower at $94.62 on Wednesday, its first close under $100 since September, after Vance blames the midterm defeat on the Iran war → markets bet Washington wants out of the war; oil down more than 14% this week sharply cuts Egypt's fuel and LNG import bill.
The pound gains 65 piasters in one session to EGP 54.77 per dollar at the CBE → falling oil and the 100 bp hike ease dollar demand; a stronger pound lowers import costs and inflation pressure.

EGX30 jumps 2.83% to 50,650.18, back above 50,000, as 197 stocks rise and foreign institutions net buy EGP 338.7 mn → peace hopes, cheaper oil and a firmer pound pull foreign money back; pharma and consumer names lead.

Iran calls the US reply to its Hormuz plan unconvincing but Qatar says both sides stay committed, and Trump tells the FT he has no immediate plans to strike → talks continue despite attacks on shipping, keeping a deal and lower energy costs in play for Egypt.
The EBRD, the IFC and Helikon each disclose about 6.9% of Banque du Caire after buying EGP 16.7 bn of shares at EGP 5.30 → anchor foreign holders give the new listing a stable shareholder base.

Democrats win both chambers of Congress in the US midterms, with CNBC projecting at least 245 House seats and at least 51 in the Senate → a divided Washington constrains Trump's agenda for the rest of his term, including war spending, as talks with Iran continue.

EGX30 rebounds 1.76% to 49,255.66 on Tuesday, ending a four-session fall, as 180 stocks rise and foreigners net buy about EGP 130 mn → a firmer pound and lower oil bring back foreign buyers; developers and Eastern Company lead while fertiliser names fall.

Gas supplies to fertilizer plants are cut 20% while Egyptian urea sells at $535 a ton, about 17% above September → LNG cargoes now cost over $100 mn each, so the state rations gas; Abu Qir confirms the cut and falls 3.59%.

Brent settles 1% lower at $103.60, its lowest close since 7 October, as traders weigh US-Iran talks → Iran calls the US reply unconvincing, but Qatar expects both sides' feedback within 36 hours; lower oil eases Egypt's import bill.

The government weighs selling a large EgyptAlum stake on the EGX before year-end, after Banque du Caire raised $658 mn → the state targets $1.5 bn of offerings this year; a new listing would add depth for brokers and investors.

Brent falls 7.6% to $104.77 on Monday, its biggest drop in three months, after Iran's supreme leader approves talks and Tehran offers to reopen Hormuz in two days → a lower oil price eases Egypt's fuel import bill and pressure on the pound, though a US strike on Qeshm Island overnight lifts Brent 0.5% in Asia.

The pound strengthens to EGP 55.51 per dollar at the CBE on Monday from 56.12 after the hike, and major banks quote 55.49 → the 100 bp hike and falling oil ease demand for dollars; a firmer pound helps importers and foreign holders of local debt.

EGX30 slips 0.70% to 48,403.14 while the EGX70 and EGX100 fall more than 2.2% and 197 stocks decline against 31 → foreigners net sell EGP 138.1 mn and Banque du Caire absorbs 21% of turnover, leaving little cash for small caps.

Banque du Caire closes its first session at EGP 5.31, up 0.19% on the EGP 5.30 offer, after touching EGP 5.68 → pricing at fair value leaves little first-day gain; the Treasury takes up to half the EGP 36.37 bn proceeds to ease debt.

Egypt's non-oil PMI stays at 47.2 in October, below a 48 forecast and its tenth straight month below 50 → output and new orders fall at the fastest pace in four months and input costs rise at a five-month high.

stories.h: Inflation eases to 12% in October as monthly price growth slows
stories.what: Annual headline inflation falls to 12% in October from 12.8% in September, CAPMAS data show, and prices rise 0.6% on the month. Food and drinks rise 0.8% on the month and 7.5% on the year, with meat and poultry up 3.2% in October. Housing, utilities and fuel are up 24.1% on the year and transport 22.3%. Planning Minister Ahmed Rostom tells the cabinet that monthly inflation has eased from 3.3% in March.
stories.why: Price pressure eases after earlier increases, while fruit and vegetable prices fall on the month.
stories.aff: Real interest rates, household spending and the CBE's next rate decision.
stories.eg: With the deposit rate at 20%, the real rate widens to about 8 points (derived), which supports the pound.
stories.egx: Bullish for banks and consumer names; it lowers the odds of another hike.

key.l: Goldman Sachs' estimate of the pound's undervaluation

stories.h: Goldman Sachs calls the pound 30% undervalued and sees 50 per dollar in a year
stories.what: Goldman Sachs keeps its buy call on the pound and says it trades more than 30% below fair value after October's slide. It now sees EGP 53 per dollar in three months, 52 in six and 50 in twelve, against 49, 48 and 46 before. Foreign holdings of local debt fall to about $20 bn from about $30 bn at end-September, which Goldman says leaves positioning lighter. "If regional tensions ease, the EGP could rally strongly," the bank says.
stories.why: Fair value, based on the real effective exchange rate, holds steady while the market rate weakens.
stories.aff: Foreign flows into T-bills, the pound and import costs.
stories.eg: A buy call from a major bank can speed the return of carry-trade money.
stories.egx: Bullish for banks and foreign-held blue chips; bearish for dollar earners if the pound rallies.

key.l: export support in the FY2026/27 budget

stories.h: Cabinet lifts export rebates by 35% and pays up to half of freight to new markets
stories.what: The cabinet approves a revamped rebate programme on Thursday that raises support by an average of 35% for shipments from the start of November. The state covers 50% of sea and land freight to Africa, Latin America, Australia, Southeast Asia and Russia, 25% of air freight to Europe and 25% of insurance. The US and 11 Southeast Asian countries join the target markets. The budget sets aside EGP 48 bn, against EGP 28 bn paid last year.
stories.why: The government wants faster export growth and more companies selling abroad; the first phase runs to the end of 2026.
stories.aff: Textiles, food, engineering, pharma, furniture, chemicals and building materials.
stories.eg: More exports bring in dollars and ease pressure on the pound.
stories.egx: Bullish for listed exporters, though arrears on old shipments remain.
stories.names: Food, textile, chemical and building-material exporters (sectors).

key.l: ships redirected by US forces since July

stories.h: US launches a task force to block Iran's land routes as blasts hit Qeshm
stories.what: CENTCOM sets up Task Force Iron Gate to stop weapons and sanctioned goods crossing Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. Admiral Brad Cooper says it reinforces the "ironclad blockade against Iran at sea." US forces disable a St Kitts-flagged ship in the Gulf of Oman and have redirected 147 vessels since July. IRNA reports blasts on Qeshm and in Bandar Abbas, and the IRGC says two tankers hit mines near Hormuz. Trump says Iran still wants a deal and Qatar's talks continue.
stories.why: Washington tightens pressure on Iran while talks run, and Iran shows it can still disrupt shipping.
stories.aff: Oil, Gulf shipping, Suez traffic and regional risk premiums.
stories.eg: A longer war keeps Egypt's energy bill and canal revenue under pressure.
stories.egx: Bearish for tourism and logistics; neutral for the wider market until talks move.

key.l: shares five EGX companies bought back last week

stories.h: Five EGX companies buy back 20.1 mn shares during the market's recovery week
stories.src: EnterpriseAM; Amwal Al Ghad; See News
stories.what: Bonyan, PRE Group, Ibnsina Pharma, Edita and Taaleem buy about 20.1 mn of their own shares between Sunday and Thursday, EnterpriseAM says; Edita's largest purchase is 1.68 mn shares on Monday. The EGX30 falls on Sunday and Monday, then rises three days to close Thursday at 51,152.73, and market cap ends at about EGP 4.05 tn. Foreigners are Thursday's only net buyers.
stories.why: Boards use October's sell-off, when the EGX30 lost 4.43%, to buy shares cheaply.
stories.aff: Mid caps with buyback programmes and their free float.
stories.eg: Buybacks add a steady buyer while foreign money is only starting to return.
stories.egx: Bullish for the companies buying back; a sign boards see value.
stories.names: Edita, Ibnsina Pharma, Taaleem, PRE Group, Bonyan (bullish).

stories.h: Nasdaq has its worst day since April 2025 on fears for the AI buildout
stories.what: The Nasdaq Composite falls 5.5% on Thursday and enters a correction, then rises 1.09% on Friday. Chipmakers drop about 12%, with AMD and Micron down 17% and Nvidia 9%. Investors fear the Democrats' midterm sweep will slow US data-centre construction; UBS estimates about 30% of capacity due in 2028 could be at risk. Gold ends at $4,075, down 0.9%.
stories.why: Local opposition over power and water use could pause data-centre projects.
stories.aff: Global tech stocks, risk appetite and emerging-market flows.
stories.eg: Egypt has little direct tech exposure, but a global risk-off mood can slow inflows.
stories.egx: Neutral; the EGX rose on Thursday while the Nasdaq fell.
